headline: Alexander-Walker has 27 points as Hawks roll to 107-97 win over Pistons in off game for Cunningham
text: ATLANTA -- — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points. Cunningham set a season high with 15 assists but a combination of early foul trouble and a sore knee combined to hold him to 20 points below his average of 25.6 as he made 2 of 9 shots. It was his first game of the season not scoring in double figures. Corey Kispert scored a season-high 18 points and Lu Dort had 16 in the Hawks' fourth straight win. Isaiah Joe led Detroit with 19 points. Ausar Thompson and John Collins had 18 and Paul Reed added 16. The Pistons led 85-74 at the start of the fourth quarter before the Hawks took a 92-85 with the 18 unanswered points. Joe's 3-pointer with 4:52 remaining ended Detroit's scoreless streak. Cunningham picked up two fouls in the first period and was called for his third foul early in the second. He was limited to 14 minutes in the first half while missing all three of his shots from the field. Cunningham scored his first points with a jumper off the glass early in the second half but continued to focus on setting up shots for teammates while receiving extra defensive attention from Dyson Daniels and the Hawks. Cunningham was included on Detroit's injury report with right knee soreness. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before the game protecting Cunningham was “the most important thing. He’s a competitor and wants to play. But it’s also our responsibility to just make sure that we’re protecting him at all costs.” Cunningham was held out of Detroit's 122-109 win at New Orleans on Wednesday night but scored 23 points in a 105-102 loss to Toronto on Friday night. Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings had 10 points after missing three games with a sore back. Up next Pistons: Play at Orlando on Tuesday night. Hawks: Visit Boston on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Adebayo gets triple-double, Heat (without Giannis) top Thunder (without SGA) for 7th straight win
text: MIAMI -- — Bam Adebayo scored 24 points and had a triple-double, Pelle Larsson scored 21 and the shorthanded Miami Heat beat the very shorthanded Oklahoma City Thunder 123-113 on Sunday night to push their winning streak to seven games. Adebayo finished with 15 rebounds and 12 assists, his ninth career triple-double in regular season play. He's also had one in the postseason. Nikola Jović scored 15 and Davion Mitchell added 14 for Miami, which had seven players in double figures. Bennett Stirtz scored 21 for Oklahoma City, which got 20 from Jared McCain , 17 from Ajay Mitchell and 13 from Josh Dix . Both teams were missing past Most Valuable Players. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander — the two-time reigning MVP — was out for Oklahoma City with a neck strain and lower back contusion, while Miami was without Giannis Antetokounmpo because of a groin strain. It was the first game missed for both Gilgeous-Alexander and Antetokounmpo this season. The Thunder, who have dealt with serious injury issues all season, had only nine available players — three of them under two-way contracts. And the Thunder never went away, getting down by 20 early in the fourth before outscoring Miami 33-23 in the final 10:36. Miami led wire-to-wire for the third consecutive game. It’s the first time in the NBA’s era of digitized play-by-play, starting in 1996, that the Heat went three straight games without trailing. The Heat became the fourth team in NBA history to improve their record to 10-6 (or better) through 16 games after an 0-4 start. The others: Dallas (12-4) in 2006-07, Oklahoma City (10-6) in 2018-19 and Sacramento (10-6) in 2022-23. Miami matched its longest win streak since a 13-game unbeaten run from Jan. 17 through Feb. 10, 2017. The Heat had three other seven-game streaks since, the most recent spanning January and February of last season. Up next Thunder: Visit Indiana on Monday. Heat: Visit Philadelphia on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Wizards rout the Magic 116-96 to win their 3rd straight following an 8-game skid
text: WASHINGTON -- — Kyshawn George scored 24 points and Anthony Davis added 22 to lead the Washington Wizards to their third straight victory, 116-96 over the Orlando Magic on Sunday night. Trae Young had 11 points and 11 assists for the Wizards, who have rebounded from an early eight-game losing streak. They won with torrid shooting Sunday, going 22 of 39 from 3-point range and never trailing after opening the game with an 11-0 run. The Wizards have won three in a row for the first time since Feb. 1-5, 2025. Tristan da Silva scored 18 points and Desmond Bane had 17 for Orlando, which was without star Paolo Banchero because of a sprained ankle. The Wizards led by as many as 20 in the first half, although it was 63-51 at the break and the Magic quickly cut it to seven in the third quarter. Washington answered with a 12-0 run that included two 3-pointers by George, one by Tre Johnson and another by Young. A 3 by Bilal Coulibaly made it 97-75 late in the third. Coulibaly scored 12 points, all on 3s. Johnson had 11 on 4-of-5 shooting. Top overall draft pick AJ Dybantsa scored 16 with eight rebounds and six assists for Washington. Franz Wagner had 16 points, eight rebounds and six assists for the Magic. Washington's franchise record for 3-pointers is 23, set in an overtime loss to Indiana on Feb. 12, 2025. Will Riley made what initially looked like the team's 23rd on Sunday, but it was ruled a 2. Up next Magic: Host Detroit on Tuesday night. Wizards: Host Boston on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jokic's triple-double, Murray's 45 points lead Nuggets to 151-145 overtime win over Bulls
text: CHICAGO -- — Nikola Jokic had 37 points, 18 rebounds and 11 assists for the 202nd triple double of his career, Jamal Murray scored eight of his season-high 45 points in overtime, and the Denver Nuggets held off the Chicago Bulls 151-145 on Sunday night. Jokic closed the gap on Russell Westbrook's NBA record of 209 career triple-doubles. Murray was 13 for 22 from the floor, 6 for 11 from 3-point range and 13 for 14 from the free-throw line. Buddy Hield scored 33 points for the short-handed Bulls and Josh Giddey bounced back from a fourth-quarter benching Friday with 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists. He is the first Bulls player with more than 20 assists in a game since 1985 and the first with a 20-point/20-assist game since Dec. 6, 1969 when Clem Haskins had 23 points and 21 assists against Boston. Hield stole the ball from Jokic with seven seconds to go and Giddey made an open layup to tie the score at 131 as the Bulls wiped out a seven-point deficit in the final 40 seconds. Jokic missed a 3-point attempt as time expired. Murray helped the Nuggets score the first eight points of overtime. The Bulls, who had won three of five after a 1-9 start, allowed 130 or more points in regulation for the fifth time this season and fell to 1-5 at home despite a season high 25 3-pointers, led by Hield with seven. Jalen Smith added a career-high 26 points for the Bulls and Matas Buzelis , who was also benched in Friday's fourth quarter, scored 21 points. The Bulls were without their two leading scorers, Norman Powell (right hamstring strain) and Caleb Wilson (fractured metacarpal), who are averaging a combined 39.7 points per game, as well as reserve forward Nic Claxton (illness). Up next Nuggets: Host Dallas on Tuesday night. Bulls: Host Cleveland on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Cooper Flagg saves Mavericks with late free throws to hold off Jazz comeback in 116-114 win
text: SALT LAKE CITY -- — Cooper Flagg scored 28 points and made the game-winning free throws with 3.7 seconds left to lift the Dallas Mavericks over the Utah Jazz 116-114 after they squandered an 18-point lead in the fourth quarter on Sunday night. Kyrie Irving scored 16 points, all in the first half, as the Mavericks (10-7) barely avoided an epic collapse and won their third in a row. Svi Mykhailiuk came off the bench to score a career-high 39 points, including 10 of 15 from beyond the arc. Mykhailiuk had 23 points in the fourth quarter to fuel Utah’s (3-15) improbable comeback. The Mavericks led 114-98 with 2:14 remaining before the Jazz reeled off 16 straight points to tie the game at 104 on Isaiah Collier 's driving layup with 4.7 seconds to play. After Flagg's clutch free throws, the Jazz couldn't get the ball to Mykhailiuk and Kyle Filipowski 's 3-point attempt missed at the buzzer. Mykhailiuk's 10 3-pointer performance is one off the Utah franchise record and is tied for the most in an NBA game this season. P.J. Washington , who posted his season-high and career-high in points against the Jazz, was out with an illness but it didn't seem to matter until Mykhailiuk's hot streak. Jaxson Hayes left the game in the second quarter with a knee injury, further decimating Utah's front line. Starting big men Lauri Markkanen (hand), Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson Jr . (knee) are still out. Flagg had eight points and Zaccharie Risacher had two dunks during a 20-5 third-quarter Mavericks run — where they beat the Jazz down the court time after time —to open up an 80-62 advantage, their largest lead of the game. Utah's 23 turnovers led to 32 points for Dallas. Up next Mavericks: Visit Denver on Tuesday night. Jazz: Visit the Lakers in Los Angeles for the second time in five days. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Karl-Anthony Towns has 30 points and 13 rebounds as Knicks beat Pacers 113-106
text: NEW YORK -- — Karl-Anthony Towns had 30 points and 13 rebounds, Jalen Brunson added 22 points, and the New York Knicks beat the Indiana Pacers 113-106 on Sunday night to extend their winning streak to five games. Towns, who missed Saturday night’s buzzer-beater victory over Portland due to an illness, shot 9 for 14 from the field including 4 for 4 on 3-pointers. Landry Shamet scored 17 points while Josh Hart finished with 10 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds for the Knicks. It was Hart's 18th triple-double with the Knicks, tying Michael Ray Richardson for second on the team’s career list. Walt Frazier holds the team record with 23. The Knicks were without OG Anunoby , who missed his second straight game because of tightness in his left calf. Backup guard Deuce McBride was held out due to tightness in the left abductor. Pascal Siakam scored 25 points, Andrew Nembhard finished with 16 and Ivica Zubac had 10 points and 14 rebounds for the Pacers, who have lost their last four games. Towns in the closing minutes of the third quarter outscored Indiana 10-2, capping it off with a 3-pointer that extended the Knicks lead 86-74 with 54 seconds left in the period. Indiana fell behind by 12 points after Mikal Bridges hit a 3-pointer that made it 92-80 and trimmed it to 95-87 following a three-point play from Kelly Oubre Jr . with 7:31 left in the fourth quarter. A fadeaway jumper from Brunson increased the Knicks advantage to 110-95 — their largest lead of the night — with 2:35 remaining. The Pacers kept it close and went on a 6-0 run capped by a layup from Obi Toppin that made it 112-106 with 25 seconds remaining. Brunson then put the game out of reach with a free throw after Quenton Jackson was called for a foul away from the ball. Up Next Pacers: Host Oklahoma City on Monday night. Knicks: Continue their five-game homestand against Cleveland on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
